faq.q: What specific material properties make Titanium Derailleur Pulley suitable for Rear derailleur guide pulley with bearing?
faq.a: Titanium Derailleur Pulley uses Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V because its yield strength, fatigue endurance, and corrosion resistance directly address derailleur hardware operational demands. The alloy's specific strength enables mass reduction without section compromise, while the TiO2 passivation ensures long-term environmental resistance.

faq.q: What are the critical dimensional tolerances for Titanium Derailleur Pulley?
faq.a: Standard machining tolerance for Titanium Derailleur Pulley is +/-0.05mm (ISO 2768-m). Functional mating surfaces are held to +/-0.025mm with Ra 0.8um finish, verified specifically for rear derailleur guide requirements. Threaded features conform to ISO 965-2 Class 6g, verified with calibrated Go/No-Go ring gauges on 100% of production.

faq.q: Does Titanium Derailleur Pulley require any post-machining surface treatment?
faq.a: Yes. rear derailleur guide components require Bead blasting 120 grit Al2O3 for matte finish Ra 1.6-3.2um followed by passive oxide stabilization in DI water — tailored for rear derailleur guide application. This restores the natural TiO2 passive layer removed during machining and provides the required surface properties for the specific service environment. Key parameters include surface finish Ra 0.8um and passive layer thickness verification per applicable standards.
